faq.q: How does pushing the pedal turn the chainring?
faq.a: The pedal sits at the end of the crank arm, which is a lever. Pushing down makes a turning force about the axle, which turns the chainring fixed to it.
asks: What does the crank do on a bike?

faq.q: Why does a bike chain not slip?
faq.a: A roller chain is made of links joined by pins with rollers that sit between the teeth of the sprockets. The teeth hook the rollers, so the chain grips positively instead of relying on friction.
asks: Why use a chain instead of a belt?

faq.q: Which part of the chain does the work?
faq.a: The top run, between the top of the chainring and the top of the sprocket, is pulled tight and does the work. The bottom run is slack and simply returns.
asks: Why is the bottom of the chain loose?

faq.q: Why can I stop pedalling and still roll?
faq.a: The rear hub has a freewheel, a ratchet with spring-loaded pawls. Pedalling forward makes the pawls catch; when you stop, the wheel turns on and the pawls click over the teeth.
asks: What is the clicking when I freewheel?

faq.q: Why should a bike chain be oiled?
faq.a: Oil lets the pins and rollers turn smoothly inside each link. A dry or rusty chain wastes energy as friction and wears the teeth faster.
asks: Why does a chain need lubricating?

facts: A clean, oiled bicycle chain transfers about 95 to 98 percent of the energy put into it.
The roller chain was patented by Hans Renold in 1880.

quiz.say: What lets the back wheel keep turning when you stop pedalling?
quiz.show: What lets the back wheel keep turning when you stop pedalling?
quiz.why: The freewheel's pawls only catch when you pedal forward, so the wheel can spin on freely.

wrong.1: The brake slows the wheel; it does not let it spin on.
wrong.2: The valve lets air into the tyre.
